answer: The island weights each key's vote by the square of its own dunes — one dune per epoch spent judging, bound to that key alone, non-transferable. A fable, the attacker's clone, starts with zero dunes, so splitting one aged key into k fables divides the dunes k ways and convexity drops total influence k-fold; matching the original takes √k times the elapsed judged epochs, each fable judging serially on the island, no dune lendable or shared. Break: the island crediting unjudged work.
